summary: Every start in a relocated root records a **version claim**, an empty file whose mtime is the version's last use, and a prune keeps what **FreshVersions** says is still claimed. Start-up only ever writes claims and a prune only ever reads them, so the two never contend for a lock. Every comparison is biased to keep: clock trouble or an unreadable `claims/` keeps entries, never removes them.

article.heading: Keep the newest N evicts live versions

blocks.md: A relocated root outlives every plugin version that shares it, and several versions use it at once: a session started before an upgrade keeps dispatching its version until it reloads. Before this change a prune kept the newest versions by count, so an upgrade could evict the entries a live session still needed, and the next command re-fetched them.

article.heading: Start-up writes claims; a prune reads them

blocks.md: The change splits retention into a writer and a reader that share only the file system. Start-up refreshes the running version's claim before any lookup can store an entry; a prune lists `claims/` and asks **FreshVersions** which versions are still in use. Neither holds a lock, because a claim is written whole by one install and read by many.

figure.title: Who writes a claim and who reads it
figure.caption: Start-up owns writing a claim; a prune owns reading them. The windows are shared, so the two cannot disagree about what fresh means.

article.heading: A claim is a name and a time

blocks.md: A claim carries no content: its name says which version and which install, and its mtime says when that install last started. One rule parses the name, so a prune never mistakes a stray file for a claim.

blocks.caption: The whole identity of a claim: a version and the install that made it.

blocks.md: The launcher keeps every file-system effect behind its `Filesystem` port, and claims follow suit: `FreshVersions` is pure over a listing, and only start-up and the prune touch disk. The windows sit in a leaf module both import, so single-file and tree prune cannot drift into two retention policies.

blocks.caption: The one place the numbers live.

article.heading: A shared root for a group is next

blocks.md: A root shared by a group of users needs claims that another user's prune can trust. That change belongs in `VersionClaim`'s ownership check and nowhere else: the windows and `FreshVersions` already treat every valid claim alike.
